_comment: Ratchet baseline for the Datastore Isolation workflow (TD-881).
These ceilings MAY ONLY EVER FALL. CI fails when a run exceeds one, which is
the signal that something new in the suite reaches the operator's real
services. When a run comes in under, lower the number so the ground gained
cannot be given back.
WHAT IS COUNTED
The gated number is data-carrying connections PLUS connections the classifier
could not decide. Undecided ones are included deliberately: a connection that
did not declare itself inside the budget might have carried data, and scoring
it as a harmless probe would let a real regression hide behind a slow runner.
See Tripwire._classify. Bare probes -- a peer that closed having sent nothing
-- are a definite outcome and are not gated.
IT IS NOT ZERO, DELIBERATELY
Zero would require every test that spawns a real hook script to be re-pointed
at a throwaway instance -- roughly eighteen more files, tracked separately as
a burn-down. What protects the operator is the network namespace: every one of
these connections lands on the tripwire inside the namespace and reaches
nothing real. These numbers measure test hygiene; the namespace is the safety.
THESE NUMBERS ARE MEASURED IN CI, AND A LOCAL RUN WILL NOT MATCH
The two environments target different ports, because a maintainer machine has
an AI-Memory install and a runner does not:
On a runner QDRANT_GRPC_PORT is unset, so qdrant-client falls back to its own
gRPC default of 6334; locally that variable is set to 26351 by the operator's
docker/.env, which src/memory/classifier/config.py loads into the environment.
Langfuse is absent on a runner, so 23100 goes quiet there while dominating
locally. Both 26351 and 6334 therefore have to be watched -- an earlier design
watched neither.
THE RULE FOR A PER-PORT CEILING: MAX ACROSS OBSERVED ENVIRONMENTS
A per-port ceiling is the highest count seen in any environment the gate runs
in -- currently a maintainer machine and a CI runner. It is NOT 'the CI number'.
The gate has to pass in both, so a ceiling set to the lower of the two would
fail the other environment for a difference that is a property of the machine
rather than a regression in the suite.
That is why 28080 is 9 and not CI's 6: 9 is the local figure and therefore the
max. 26350 is 4 because both environments agree on 4 -- there is no spread to
take a maximum over, which is exactly what makes it the port worth gating
tightly. When a new environment is added, raise a ceiling only to that
environment's observed value, and record it in this file alongside the others.
A ceiling still may only fall when EVERY environment comes in below it.
26350 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS
It is the Qdrant REST port -- the one tests actually write through -- and it
measured exactly 4 on both a runner and a maintainer machine. max_per_port
gates it exactly, so a new test reaching the datastore fails immediately, with
no whole-suite headroom for it to hide inside.
Before this work the same measurement was 147 accepts / 122 data-carrying
across the three ports then being watched, with 101 on 26350. Measured on the
CI-scope suite (-m 'not regression and not quarantine') with a cleared
environment, inside a network namespace, ordering fixed via -p no:randomly.
A CEILING NEEDS A FLOOR UNDER IT
min_executed is not a ratchet -- it is what stops the ratchet grading a run
that never happened. Every ceiling here is satisfied most easily by a suite
that does not execute: it connects to nothing, so it scores zero.
THE FLOOR COUNTS EXECUTED TESTS, NOT COLLECTED ONES
The key used to be min_tests and it counted COLLECTED tests -- JUnit's `tests`
attribute, which includes skips. That made this gate an instance of the defect
it exists to catch: a run in which all ~6,500 tests collected and every single
one skipped satisfied a floor of 5000 and passed. The gate was satisfiable
without the property it stood for (BUG-535 / BUG-536, GR-01).
It is now `executed = tests - skipped`, evaluated by tests/ci_executed_floor.py
-- the same checker every other suite-running job uses, so the basis cannot
drift between them. A baseline still carrying `min_tests` is rejected loudly
rather than ignored, because a silently-vanishing floor is how this started.
The number below is MEASURED, not chosen. A CI run of this job reported
6556 collected, 684 skipped -> 5872 EXECUTED. The floor of 5000 clears that
by about 15%: wide enough that a few tests legitimately skipping does not
flake the gate, tight enough that a partial selection or a mass-skip fails
instead of setting a new best score. For scale, a BUG-535-shaped loss (a
third of the suite skipped away) would execute ~3900 and fail this floor.
Note the collected count ROSE from the 6486-6503 recorded before this
migration while the executed count is lower, which is the whole point: the
old key was reading the larger, less meaningful number. Raise this when the
suite grows; a floor that trails far behind the real count stops catching
partial selections. See check_run_happened.
WHY THERE IS NO WHOLE-SUITE TOTAL GATE ANY MORE
There was one -- max_gated, with a jitter allowance -- and it was retired
because it could not detect the thing it existed for.
Its stated job was to catch a port nobody thought to watch. It cannot. The
tripwire binds only the ports in PRODUCTION_PORTS, and it cannot count traffic
to a port it never bound, so the total is by construction the sum of the
per-port counts. An unwatched port is unbound, contributes zero, and moves the
total not at all. The total therefore caught nothing the per-port ceilings did
not already catch.
Meanwhile it carried all of the variance. Across three green CI runs it read
25, 38 and 37 against a ceiling of 40, and every bit of that spread was one
port: 6334 measured 15, 28 and 27 while 26350 held at 4 and 28080 at 6 in every
run. A gate that cannot catch its own quarry but CAN false-trip on retry noise
is worse than no gate: it gets raised, raised again, and then ignored.
What replaces it is not a looser number. tests/test_datastore_guard.py asserts
that every port the tripwire binds carries a ceiling here. That answers 'did we
forget to gate something' directly instead of by proxy, cannot false-trip, and
fails the moment a port is added to PRODUCTION_PORTS without one. The total is
still printed by the ratchet as a trend line; nothing fails on it.
WHY 6334 IS LOOSE AND 26350 IS EXACT
6334 is qdrant-client's own gRPC default, reached only when QDRANT_GRPC_PORT is
unset -- which is the normal state on a runner and never the case on a machine
with an install. Its count is connection-retry churn, not distinct test
behaviour: one client retrying is several accepts. That is why it is 45 against
an observed 15-28 rather than pinned. Do not tighten it toward the observed
figure; the spread is the point.
26350 is the opposite and is pinned at exactly 4. It is the REST port the suite
actually writes through, and it measured 4 on a runner and 4 on a maintainer
machine, every run. Nothing about it jitters, so any movement is a real change.
That pin is the gate doing the real work.
26351 and 23100 are ceilinged at their local figures, which are their maxima --
both are absent on a runner (no install, no Langfuse) and so read 0 there.
